---

## The Core Claim

The economically relevant knowledge needed to allocate resources efficiently is not held by any single planner but is dispersed as fragmentary, time-and-place-specific information across millions of individual economic actors; a market price system functions as a decentralized information-aggregation and transmission mechanism, compressing this dispersed knowledge into a single signal -- the price -- without requiring any actor to know more than their own local circumstances plus the price. Friedrich Hayek won the 1974 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for pioneering work on the interdependence of economic, social, and institutional phenomena, this dispersed-knowledge account of markets central among it.
